notes.summary: BJ v4 already constructs the genuine singular finite-energy operator with raw mass V, intrinsic dual-energy targets, comparison and uniqueness. Its existence theorem remains conditional on EP.
notes.detailedSummary: The primary-source scope includes reduced nonnormal projective varieties over algebraically closed trivially valued fields. In the retained characteristic-zero, integral, ample-line-bundle domain, raw MA has mass V=(L^n), finite dual energy is equivalent to integrability of every E1 potential, and uniqueness modulo constants and domination precede envelopes. Variational attainment requires EP compactness and bounded-J target integration continuity. The new singular EP claim is not accepted by citation.
notes.text:
Primary-source partial theorem. Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero; X reduced irreducible projective; L ample; omega=c1(L), n=dim X and V=(L^n)>0. No normality or measure-support restriction is used in the following operator, target condition or uniqueness assertions. This retains the original geometrically unibranch equation domain but does not prove existence on it.

BJ defines reduced, possibly nonnormal varieties at LF450–469 and resumes general projective varieties at LF3649–3658. Its test configurations are closed integrally INSIDE THE PRESCRIBED GENERIC FIBER, rather than absolutely normalized (Definition1.10 and Theorem1.13, LF759–849). The polar-ideal determinant trick forces associated vertical poles to be DVRs; vertical depth two excludes higher-codimension poles. This preserves a nonnormal generic fiber. On a common relative closure, the genuine raw mixed model measure is sum_E b_E product_i((theta_i,model+D_i)|E) delta_vE, with b_E=ord_E(t)>0 and v_E=b_E^(-1)ord_E restricted to k(X). Nef restrictions give nonnegative weights. The central fundamental cycle and rational equivalence to the generic fiber give mass (theta_1…theta_n)_X, retaining all multiplicities.

The compactified symmetric intersection pairing is determination-independent by projection formula; translation adds c times the other classes’ mixed degree. Extend it by infimum over model majorants. Monotonicity is intersection positivity. For upper semicontinuity, select a majorant tuple below a strict pairing threshold; continuity of sup(phi_i−psi_i) supplies nearby translated majorants, and the translation rule bounds the error. Decreasing-net continuity follows. Mixed energy bounds extend it multilinearly to finite-energy differences. Define E(phi)=pairing((omega,phi)^(n+1))/((n+1)V), E(0)=0, E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c, and E1={genuine omega-PSH phi:E(phi)>−infinity}. Pairing with (0,a), for actual algebraic PL tests, defines integration. Positivity bounds its norm by mass times ||a||; PL density and Radon representation construct the genuine mixed measure (BJ7.18–7.19 LF3980–4057), with exact mass, model agreement, mixed integrability and decreasing continuity. Probability MA=raw MA/V.

Weighted7.21 needs an explicit sign correction: integral phi_0 dM equals the pairing containing phi_0 MINUS the zero-test pairing, correctly printed at LF4107–4113; LF4119–4123 reverse these terms. Both corrected pairings converge. Translate the test below zero and apply the positive weighted-measure lemma to its negative. Model winning-component equality passes to E1 by applying weighted continuity separately to max(phi_j,psi_j) and psi_j; their difference need not decrease. Thus 1_{phi>psi} MA(max(phi,psi))=1_{phi>psi} MA(phi). Displaced maxima and equal masses give integral_{phi<psi} MA(psi)<=integral_{phi<psi} MA(phi). This supplies the weighted argument missing from the last citation at LF4585 without assuming measure monotonicity.

For I(phi,psi)=integral(phi−psi)(MA(psi)−MA(phi)), mixed negativity gives I>=0. BJ10.3 separation, tested against finite-energy divisorial Diracs and the trivial Dirac, forces equal divisorial values when I=0 and suprema agree. Divisorial determination gives equality everywhere: actual Corollary10.4 LF5444–5456. Equal measures therefore imply one additive real constant. Actual Corollary10.6 LF5468–5477 proves domination before EP: replace phi by max(phi,psi) under phi<=psi MA(psi)-almost everywhere. The replacement has nonpositive I with psi, hence a constant difference; almost-everywhere equality removes that constant.

A raw target nu is positive Radon with mass V. For mu=nu/V, its exact intrinsic condition is E^vee(mu)=sup_{psi in E1}(E(psi)−integral psi dmu)<infinity. BJ9.20 LF5266–5301 equates this with integrability of EVERY E1 potential on integral X. The proof mechanism is explicit: if integration were unbounded below on normalized J=−E<=C, select psi_j with integrals <=−2^j. The decreasing convex sums sum_{j<=m}2^(−j)psi_j have energy >=−C and converge to an E1 potential with integral −infinity, contradiction. Mixed expansion gives J(tpsi)<=C_n t²J(psi); scaling yields −integral psi<=A sqrt(J)+B and finite dual energy. Actual outputs satisfy this condition by mixed integrability and the concave tangent inequality. No support restriction enters.

Actual BJ8.5 LF4843–4960 gives the unconditional outer expansion E-down(phi+tf)=E(phi)+t integral f MA(phi)+O_f(t²), uniform in phi, for PL f. Fixed mixed degrees bound the error; both signs and uniform PL approximation give continuous directions. The upper endpoint of the printed LF4954 squeeze must be integral f_m MA+epsilon_m, not minus epsilon_m. For unbounded phi, identifying outer energy with energy of the genuine envelope requires EP. BJ’s relative-volume inputs cited outside the ten caches are used through its primary theorem, not independently reproved here.

Under genuine EP, BJ5.11 LF2819–2842 proves normalized-PSH compactness through bounded divisorial evaluations, Tychonoff, genuine tail upper envelopes and divisorial nonnegligibility. A dual maximizing sequence has bounded J by9.15. Its weak subnet limit has finite energy by J lower semicontinuity. Proposition9.19 LF5245–5262 supplies L1(mu) convergence by uniform bounded-J approximation with integrations against maximizing model MA measures, before attainment. Its scalar identity is |a−b|=2max(a,b)−a−b, correcting LF5254. Energy upper semicontinuity gives an ACTUAL maximizer. Both signs in outer differentiation and duality then give the genuine equation. The raw objective VE−integral phi dnu is translation invariant exactly at mass V.

Consequently every intrinsic target has a genuine solution, unique modulo constants, IF EP holds. Actual BJ12.8 LF6092–6141 equates EP, onto MA and E1 completeness;12.9 LF6144–6146 is the smooth sufficient endpoint. Operator construction and strict concavity do not establish singular EP. Dimension zero is immediate: one point, V=1 and E(c)=c.

notes.summary: Explicit extended-coordinate strict barriers and genuine AFS approximants are reconstructed, including individual floors for real supports. Original-ring hull localization uses actual normalization pole orders.
notes.detailedSummary: The soft maximum has a unique strict support and a uniform gap off every neighborhood, including infinite coordinates. Multinomial approximants are globally uniform and retain generators. Real coefficients use individual logarithm floors and nested rational intervals. A countable strict potential has an explicit decreasing diagonal. Localization uses finite normalization only for divisor orders, integrality of h^p f^q, and one f^N annihilator in the original ring. Limit hull comparison still requires controlled approximation.
notes.text:
Independent proof drafts, with n1 fixing the meaning of the genuine global cone. Work over the retained algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k. Actual rational affine FS (AFS) means max(lambda,c_i log|f_i|+C_i), with rational constants, positive rational coefficients, and a list containing algebra generators of the ORIGINAL affine ring. Positive rational sums and maxima are AFS after distributing maxima; floors in other factors retain generator branches. A power branch can be supplemented identically by a low original-generator branch: for 0<eta<c, sufficiently large M gives eta log|z|−M<=max(lambda,c log|z|+C) at every norm, including zero. Upper growth always means u<=H+C. Corrected contact positivity requires b(s)>=ell(s)+C and equality at t with the SAME C. These auxiliary definitions do not redefine genuine PSH.

For T_N=(R union {+infinity})^N choose integer a>=log(N+1) and chi(t)=a^(-1)log(1+sum exp(−a t_i)), with exp(−a infinity)=0. It is continuous and lies between max(0,−t_i) and that maximum+1. At t, let I be its finite coordinates, Z=1+sum_I exp(−a t_i), p_0=1/Z and p_i=exp(−a t_i)/Z. The support ell_t(s)=chi(t)−sum_I p_i(s_i−t_i) has zero coefficients at infinite coordinates and value −infinity if a used coordinate becomes infinite. Convexity gives chi>=ell. The Hessian a(diag p−pp^T) is positive definite since p_0>0, and adding any finite coordinate formerly at infinity strictly increases chi. Equality occurs only at t.

For the uniform gap, chi(s)−ell(s)>=max(0,−s_i:i in I)+sum_I p_i s_i−C_t. Its homogeneous part is positive on every nonzero vector: the weighted average of 0,−s_i with ALL positive weights p_0,p_i is strictly below their maximum unless they all vanish. Compactness of the unit sphere gives coercivity. A bounded gap sublevel confines finite I-coordinates to bounded intervals; bounded chi and ell then bound the other coordinates below, allowing their infinity endpoints. These are closed compact sublevels in the extended product, with unique zero t. A positive minimum outside any neighborhood of t, combined with the sublevel bound outside that compact set, proves a uniform positive gap. If I is empty, chi directly bounds all coordinates below and the same argument applies.

Put z_0=1,z_i=exp(−at_i). The multinomial expansion has B_m=binom(m+N,N) nonnegative terms. Their maximum lies between (sum z_i)^m/B_m and (sum z_i)^m. Hence q_m=max_{|beta|=m}{−sum_{i>0}(beta_i/m)t_i+log binom(m;beta)/(am)} satisfies q_m<=chi<=q_m+log(B_m)/(am) on the ENTIRE extended product. At poles those terms are −infinity, while beta_0=m supplies the zero floor. After t_i=−log|f_i|, each term is (1/m)log|product f_i^beta_i| plus its intercept; beta_i=1,beta_0=m−1 retains each actual generator. Choose m_j with error<=epsilon_j/4, round intercepts upward with error<=epsilon_j/4 and add rational epsilon_j, with epsilon_{j+1}<=epsilon_j/4. Values lie between chi+3epsilon_j/4 and chi+5epsilon_j/4. Thus these actual AFS functions decrease globally and converge uniformly to chi.

For a real support sum p_i log|f_i|+C, omit zero coefficients. Choose rational AFS H>=1 containing the original generators and integers D_i>=1 with log|f_i|<=D_iH. Set F_ij=max(log|f_i|,2^(-j)H−j). These are actual AFS, decrease to the individual logs including poles, and satisfy F_ij<=D_iH. Choose nested rational intervals 0<=q_ij<=p_i<=r_ij, with q increasing and r decreasing to p_i, and rational C_j decreasing to C. Let eta_j=sum D_i(r_ij−q_ij) and L_j=sum q_ij F_ij+(eta_j+2^(-j))H+C_j. The coefficient error costs at most eta_jH; negative logs improve the lower-bound inequality, so L_j majorizes the support. Moreover eta_j−eta_{j+1}>=sum D_i(q_i,j+1−q_ij). Expanding L_j−L_{j+1}, using F_ij>=F_i,j+1 and F_i,j+1<=D_iH, proves nonnegativity. The positive 2^(-j)H and the INDIVIDUAL floors retain original generator growth.

At a zero of f_i with p_i>0, q_ij is eventually positive and q_ijF_ij tends to −infinity, while other terms remain bounded above at that point. Thus the limit is exact on the support’s pole set. Flooring only the whole sum fails: on A2_{z,w}, max(p log|z|,−j)=−j along z=0 as |w| tends to infinity, so it cannot retain a positive w-generator branch.

For countable k, enumerate the affine ring, retaining generators in each finite tropicalization. These maps generate the topology. Degree bounds give rational gamma_j>0 with 0<=gamma_j chi_j<=2^(-j)(H+1). The sum rho is continuous locally uniformly and has upper logarithmic growth. T_r=sum_{j<=r}gamma_j chi_j+2^(-r)(H+1) decreases. Approximate its finite continuous sum uniformly globally by AFS A_r with errors epsilon_r=4^(-r); adding B_r=2sum_{i>=r}epsilon_i gives a decreasing sequence since the consecutive difference is >=epsilon_r−epsilon_{r+1}>0. For a neighborhood B of x, replace one finite tropical chi term by its support at x. The resulting rho-prime equals rho at x, is <=rho, and <=rho−delta outside B. Regularize that ONE support by the decreasing L_r above, approximate the remaining finite continuous terms uniformly, retain the same decreasing tail and add B_r. The decreasing support and error shifts prove monotonicity; bounded other terms prove the exact −infinity limit on its divisor. No uniform approximation at logarithmic poles or singular EP is used. This countable construction is not arbitrary-cardinality EP.

Original-ring pole-order localization: let A be integral affine, f nonzero, h in A_f, U actual AFS on Spec A, and a log|h|+b<=max(U,−c log|f|)+C on Y_f, with a,c>0. On a height-one divisor D of the finite normalization, regular elements of A have nonnegative orders. Evaluating on rays r ord_D and dividing by r gives a max(−ord_D h,0)<=c ord_D f. For positive integers p,q with q/p>c/a, z=h^pf^q has no height-one poles and lies in the normalization; it is integral over A and also belongs to A_f. The finite module A[z]/A vanishes after inverting f, so ONE f^N kills it. Therefore f^Nz^l=f^(N+ql)h^(pl) belongs to the ORIGINAL A for every l>=1.

For compact L in Y_f and x in its ORIGINAL A-polynomial hull also in Y_f, take |log|f||<=M on L union {x}. Apply hull inequalities to these regular polynomials, divide by pl, let l tend to infinity, then q/p decrease to c/a. This gives a log|h(x)|+b<=sup_L(a log|h|+b)+2cM. If h(x)=0 it is immediate. If h vanishes on L, the same tests force h(x)=0 because f(x) is nonzero. No normalization hull or subtraction of infinities is used. Denominator counting is false already for f=z²,h=z^(-1)=z/f,a=2,c=1: the original growth bound holds with U=max(0,2log|z|), but a times denominator exponent1<=c fails. Actual orders give 2 times1=1 times2.

For already regularizable v on Y_f with upper growth U+C, IF controlled approximants w_i decreasing to v satisfy w_i<=2max(U,−epsilon log|f|)+B_i, apply the proved inequality branchwise with pole budget2epsilon. Then w_i(x)<=sup_Lw_i+4epsilon M. Nested compact superlevel sets imply sup_Lw_i decreases to sup_Lv, including a limit of −infinity; no Dini-to-usc claim is needed. Passing i and then epsilon to zero proves v(x)<=sup_Lv. This LIMIT hull comparison retains its unproved controlled-approximation antecedent.

notes.summary: The split-piece Runge proof is repaired conditionally, preserving hull neighborhoods, one witness, whole-base trace continuity and gamma=1. Strict Hartogs radii and finite-projection geometry are reconstructed; analytic gates remain unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: The conditional proof localizes the integer trace near the tested fiber and places every later boundary compact inside that preimage. Both K∩Z and K\Z have uniform negative trace bounds. Witness gluing and source generators are retained. Runge precedes coefficient-radius calculations. The finite projection treats all residue conjugates and proves local isomorphism by a finite-cokernel Nakayama argument. Reduced descending inductions and empty-Z globalization remain conditional on explicit metric, controlled, smooth and trace antecedents.
notes.text:
Conditional reconstruction using n1 and n2, not acceptance of the embedded round70 or round79 proofs. Work over countable algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k. Required analytic antecedents are: (A) actual AFS references admit ample rational compactifications on the original affine chart; continuous rational contact compact perturbations and whole-collar glued metrics are genuine PSH and AFS-regularizable; controlled approximation in n2’s exact form, genuine decreasing closure and already-genuine same-class sequential regularization with section/generator conversion hold; (B) smooth weak upper-growth regularization and principal-open removal hold, including removed-set equality on the original witness; (C) finite maps pi:Y→S, with Y integral affine and S a smooth affine open in A^n, have genuine regularizable traces for all weak upper-growth inputs with one witness. Their input-independent weights m_y(s) are positive INTEGERS summing to generic degree d at every analytic fiber; on AFS tests the trace is the whole-base continuous extended determinant norm. Boundary radial identification over every completed residue field is included. These complete antecedents are NOT proved anew here.

Under A, Rossi’s boundary lemma says that x in hull_Y(L) outside L and relatively compact open B about x disjoint from L imply x in hull_Y(partial B∩hull_Y(L)). Its continuous compact-perturbation proof separates the compact bad boundary by finitely many original polynomials, adds generator bounds to an AFS function zero on the hull and positive there, multiplies it until it wins over the separating logarithm on the whole boundary, glues the maximum inside B and the reference outside through a whole winning collar, then uses a uniformly accurate AFS approximant on the compact hull to contradict the hull inequality. This does not assume weak singular regularization.

Let u be weak upper-growth and ORIGINAL u already locally regularizable on affine opens covering Y outside Z. With rho from n2, the localized implication is (u+c rho)(x)<=sup_L(u+c rho) for x in hull_Y(L) outside Z. If it fails, add small rational epsilon times v=max_i log|f_i| for ideal generators of Z. Individual floors regularize v with pole set Z. The perturbed upper semicontinuous function attains a finite maximum at y outside L and Z. Choose B with closure in one principal regularization chart, disjoint from L, and replace rho by n2’s support bump rho-prime. The sum q=u+c rho-prime+epsilon v is regularizable there by the ORIGINAL-u hypothesis and has a strict boundary gap containing c times the bump gap. Rossi and n2’s controlled limit hull comparison contradict it. A hypothesis only about u+c rho would not allow subtraction of c rho.

Assume pi restricted to Z is a closed immersion, and Z-prime=pi^(-1)pi(Z) outside Z is closed and disjoint from Z. If {u+c rho<0} is not Runge, select compact L within it, normalize the finite hull maximum to zero at x, and choose rational delta>0 with sup_L(u+c rho)<=−delta. The localized implication forces x into Z. The polynomial hull C of {pi(x)} lies in pi(Z), since every polynomial vanishing on that image vanishes on C. Its preimage splits into compact pieces in Z and Z-prime. Disjoint neighborhoods A1,A2 avoid the opposite closed pieces; proper closedness gives an initial base neighborhood A of C whose preimage lies in their union.

Choose finitely many polynomial constraints with STRICT margins on C, including generator bounds, whose compact closed intersection Q lies in A. Rational margin normalization gives actual AFS g>=0 with Q={g<=1} and g=0 on an open U about C. Keep this original g,Q,A fixed. Put W={g<1}, W_i=pi^(-1)W∩A_i; these are open with compact closures. Let h=1 on W1 and0 on W2. Glue h-tilde=max(3g∘pi−1,h) on pi^(-1)W and 3g∘pi−1 elsewhere. For g>2/3 the outer reference wins on both pieces, a whole collar. A supplies continuous genuine AFS approximants.

Whole-base trace continuity follows from C, not from continuity on a flat open. On any compact base neighborhood E, decreasing continuous approximants converge uniformly on compact pi^(-1)E. Positivity and total degree give ||N a−N b||_E<=d||a−b||_pi^(-1)E. Every AFS trace is continuous by its extended determinant formula, so their locally uniform limit is continuous everywhere. On U the trace is an integer sum of W1 weights, hence LOCALLY constant. Choose O about pi(x) where it equals gamma; do not claim constancy on disconnected U.

If gamma>1, upper semicontinuity supplies a neighborhood N of x in W1 on which u+c rho<delta/[2(gamma−1)]. The W1 fiber at pi(x) is only x, since A1 avoids Z-prime. W1 is clopen in pi^(-1)O. Proper closedness shrinks O to O-prime so its ENTIRE W1 preimage lies in N. If gamma=1 omit this estimate. Choose B with compact closure inside W1∩pi^(-1)O-prime, disjoint from L. Consequently K=partial B∩hull_Y(L), and EVERY W1 point in its base fibers, lie in the same shrunk region with that fixed gamma. The initial polynomial hull neighborhood and gluing domains remain unchanged.

Use rho-prime from n2 at x in B and set u-prime=u+c rho-prime. It equals0 at x and is <=−e-prime on K, with e-prime>0 INCLUDING c. Let v=u-prime on W1 and0 on W2. Choose rational C0>sup_pi^(-1)Q max(u-prime,0)+delta+1 and glue v-tilde=max(C0g∘pi−delta,v) on pi^(-1)W, with the reference outside. A whole collar before g=1 is reference-winning. Weak membership uses the SINGLE ORIGINAL proper witness for u: pull back rho-prime and g, form maxima on the two disjoint pieces and glue where they agree with the reference. No unrelated witnesses are glued. The finite floor ensures generic finiteness and the displayed bound gives upper growth.

Over O-prime, v-tilde=max(u-prime,−delta) on W1 and0 on W2. C makes w=N v-tilde regularizable on S. Its finite pullback retains source generators: a monic integral equation z^m+sum_{i<m}b_i z^i=0 gives log|z|<=max_i log|b_i|/(m−i). Polynomial degree bounds and base AFS generator lower growth permit low positive source-generator branches to be appended without changing each pulled AFS function. Rossi gives x in hull_Y(K); actual decreasing AFS hull inequalities give 0=w(pi(x))<=sup_K w∘pi.

For y in K∩Z, its W1 fiber is the singleton y of weight gamma, so its trace is <=−gamma min(delta,e-prime). For y in K outside Z, the ORIGINAL localized implication yields u-prime(y)<=−delta. Its own positive weight contributes at most −delta. If gamma>1, other W1 weights total at most gamma−1 and their values are <delta/[2(gamma−1)], while W2 contributes0, so trace<=−delta/2. If gamma=1 there is NO other positive-weight W1 point, giving trace<=−delta. These uniform negative bounds on both compact pieces contradict the hull inequality. Thus the split-piece conclusion holds under A–C. With rho>=0, rational c decreasing to0 gives an increasing union of Runge sublevels equal to {u<0}; every compact lies in one member, proving the union Runge.

Independently, on an ALREADY RUNGE open D in (Y×A1)^an containing the zero section, countability gives a compact exhaustion. Compact hulls lie in D. Polynomial separation from the bad complement in larger generator boxes gives an increasing exhaustion by STRICT polynomial opens Q_i={|g_ij|<exp(b_ij)} with compact closed bounds inside D, each preceding bound strictly inside the next. Include base generators and w. For g_ij=sum_l f_ijl(y)w^l, where (y,0) lies in Q_i, the exact disk radius is −log d_Qi(y)=max_{j,l>=1}(log|f_ijl(y)|−b_ij)/l. Constant coefficients satisfy strict constraints; every fiber disk obeys the weighted Gauss bound, and Gauss points at arbitrary positive radii over H(y) prove the converse. The w bound provides a finite floor; dominated generator branches give local AFS expressions on a common compact base box. Every closed disk of radius r<d_D(y) is compact in D and hence lies in some Q_i. Thus these expressions decrease to −log d_D, including −infinity. Runge precedes this calculation. The interior of {|1|<=1} is the whole space, whereas {|1|<1} is empty, disproving the printed weak-interior identity.

Independently, the finite projection lemma is reconstructed over any infinite characteristic-zero K. Compactify integral affine n-dimensional Y in P^d, d>n, and enlarge the reduced closure of proper closed Z, smooth at closed z, by the boundary. At EACH finite separable residue conjugate of z, avoid secant lines to this enlarged set and tangent directions. Their closures have dimension at most dim(enlarged Z)+1<=n<d. Avoid X and lines between distinct conjugates. Their finite invariant union is proper and descends to K; an infinite field has a rational center outside it. Projection is finite because a positive-dimensional line fiber would contain its center in X. On the enlarged set it has a singleton geometric fiber and injective tangent map. At its finite local image algebra A→B, tangent injectivity gives m_B=m_A B+m_B²; Nakayama gives m_B=m_A B, so the fiber is its residue field. Distinct conjugate images prevent residue collapse. The finite cokernel B/A has zero fiber, hence Nakayama gives (B/A)_mA=0 and a local isomorphism to the SCHEME IMAGE. Iterate to P^n, remove the closed boundary image, choose affine target S inside a standard A^n chart, and restrict the source to the ACTUAL pi^(-1)S. This produces a finite surjection with Z restriction a closed immersion.

With A–C, reduced sets Z_{j+1}=Z_j∩closure(pi^(-1)pi(Z_j) outside Z_j) have strictly decreasing dimension: maximal-dimensional Z_j components are components of the finite preimage and are absent from the closure of complementary components. Outside pi^(-1)pi(Z_{j+1}) the split pieces are closed and disjoint. Apply the product split theorem and Hartogs conversion on actual affine base preimages. Points over pi(Z_{j+1}) outside Z_{j+1} lie outside original Z by injectivity and retain the original local hypothesis. Successive REDUCED singular strata also terminate. The smooth stratum uses B; each next smooth stratum uses the proved projection lemma. Finally Z=empty supplies the global sublevel Runge property, and the product Hartogs conversion gives global regularization.

Conversion first forms max(u−2H,M) on a common box where u−2H<=−H. Nested compact superlevel sets provide a whole eventual winning collar for continuous radius approximants. A proves genuine same-ample-class membership BEFORE sequential regularization. These inductions are conditional, not the missing EP theorem. Projective weak/genuine equality would follow from actual ample chart weights rho_i, damping by (c−1)rho_i, whole boundary collars, max_i(−rho_i)=0 and class closure as c decreases to1.

Countable singular EP still requires resolved-nef connected-fiber constancy and divisorial upper semicontinuous descent. Arbitrary cardinality further requires finite-data descent, actual relative generic-fiber closure and positive MA base change. Only individual finite PL/model competitors descend to larger countable fields. With orthogonality and positive pushforward, contact support and genuine domination would prove the large-field envelope; arbitrary competitors do not descend together. Onto normalization requires TARGET-side approaching EP in BJ5.13 before transporting E1 and measures.

The printed lower-growth smooth affine theorem has a counterexample, without refuting a corrected upper-growth theorem or final singular EP. Original hypotheses and completion criteria are unchanged. The printed lower-growth Wu4.19 is false. On A1 take v=(max(log|z|,0))² and g=max(log|z|,0). On |z|<exp(M), rational M>0, nested dyadic secants of t² on [−M,0], extended by0 for t>=0 including infinity, decrease through continuous convex rational PL functions to v after t=−log|z|. They meet the local finite-chart condition, proving local psh. Since r<=r²+1/4 for r>=0, g<=v+1/4 satisfies the printed lower-growth Definition3.15 LF766–768. On the Gauss ray |z|=exp(s),s>=0, every polynomial log norm is its degree times s, so each global AFS is <=As+B. A decreasing global AFS sequence would have a first term majorizing s² everywhere, impossible. This disproves the printed proposition, NOT a corrected upper-growth theorem or the final singular EP assertion. Wu7.1 LF2716–2717 explicitly invokes weak/global6.5, so its endpoint cannot be accepted without repaired antecedents.
